transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Anita Patel (Highbar CTO), Samir Rao (Highbar ML Eng), Emily Novak (Highbar VP Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery to align on Highbar's time-to-first-token needs, security constraints, and whether to start with Redwood Hosted (PLG quicklaunch) or a Private pilot (VPC/on-prem). Customer is evaluating cost/latency tradeoffs and regulatory needs; wants a 2-week pilot scope and a benchmark plan.

Topics:
- Quicklaunch credits and expected TTFT (time-to-first-token)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope, success criteria, timeline
- Competitor comparison and pricing expectations

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team. Appreciate you taking the time. Luis, do you want to intro quick on the technical side?
[00:18] Luis Ortega: Yeah hi hi, Luis here SE. I'll be running the bench stuff if we move forward, and uh helping scope the pilot.
[00:28] Anita Patel: Thanks, yeah I'm Anita, CTO at Highbar. We're evaluating options to get our chat assistant out to customers but we have, you know, regulatory constraints and some on-prem data we can't send to third parties.
[00:40] Samir Rao: Samir - ML eng. Main question is can we get to a reliable inference endpoint with low latency and predictable cost? Also curious about fine-tuning vs prompt engineering.
[00:52] Emily Novak: Emily here. Product wants to know TTFT — are we talking hours or weeks to first meaningful result?
[01:05] Maya Chen: Great, that's exactly what this call is for. High-level: Redwood offers a hosted API quicklaunch with free credits — that's PLG path, time-to-first-token usually within an hour for a basic test, and a Dedicated/Private option for predictable throughput and VPC connectivity. We'll talk tradeoffs.
[01:35] Anita Patel: Okay, so the quicklaunch is attractive for speed, but we can't send sensitive docs off-prem. Is there an option where we can test locally?
[01:48] Luis Ortega: Yeah so two paths: 1) Hosted API — fastest, uses Redwood's catalog (we have Redwood model variants and caching), you get free credits to experiment; 2) Private — we can run a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem package, that'll be isolated and can integrate with your KMS/HSM.
[02:10] Samir Rao: If we do Private, how long to spin up? Weeks?
[02:18] Luis Ortega: Typical private pilots take 2-4 weeks to stand up depending on infra and networking. For a minimal pilot we can usually do a two-week scoped run: deploy inference containers into your VPC, hook up our control plane, run a limited workload.
[02:35] Emily Novak: And downtime/ops burden? We don't want an ops-heavy thing for a small team.
[02:42] Maya Chen: Totally. For pilots we handle most of the heavy lifting. Private pilots include an installation runbook and remote assist from our Eng team. Dedicated/Reserved is more managed by us; Private on-prem needs a bit more customer infra.
[03:00] Anita Patel: About costs — can you ballpark cost for 10k tokens/day on hosted vs private?
[03:08] Luis Ortega: On hosted, with credits, initial cost is minimal until credits are used; then it's per-token pricing. For 10k tokens/day, rough hosted cost maybe in the low hundreds per month depending on model. Private has infra costs — GPU instances — but can be cheaper at scale. I'll send a more concrete model.
[03:34] Samir Rao: Latency matters — most of our flows need <250ms for short responses. Can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[03:43] Luis Ortega: Depends on model and region. For shorter sequences and small models it's achievable; we also have routing policies and lower-latency dedicated pools. Caching and batching interplay matter — batching helps throughput but can add latency. We can instrument and tune per route.
[04:05] Anita Patel: Security checklist — do you have SOC2/ISO artifacts? SSO? RBAC?
[04:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II, ISO docs - I'll share the pack. We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and customer-managed KMS integration for private deployments. Audit logs available in the Console.
[04:34] Emily Novak: Good. For compliance we need data residency too — can private keep everything in our region?
[04:41] Luis Ortega: Yes, Private can be deployed in your cloud region or on-prem. We also support per-request routing to keep data in-region for Hosted if needed, but that involves contractual terms.
[05:02] Samir Rao: One technical worry: our prompts include PII and long context windows — what's the max seq length and token handling?
[05:10] Luis Ortega: Our runtime supports large context models; sequence length depends on model. We also have KV cache management and prefix caching to reduce repeated token cost. For very long contexts we recommend model variants or chunking.
[05:34] Anita Patel: Competitors — we're also looking at Anthropic and OpenAI and a self-managed option with Run.ai. How are you different?
[05:44] Maya Chen: Good question. Redwood focuses on production inference economics — you get predictable routing and observability: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, and rollouts. We also offer a unified interface across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private so you don't rewrite your app when you upgrade.
[06:08] Emily Novak: Can you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback if a model variant fails?
[06:15] Luis Ortega: Yes — rollouts are built into Console: canaries, A/B tests, and fallback to compatible model variants. That helps mitigate regressions.
[06:30] Anita Patel: For the pilot, we need success criteria. What do you suggest?
[06:36] Maya Chen: Typically customers set 3 criteria: 1) performance — median latency under target (e.g., <250ms) on sample prompts, 2) cost — cost per session below threshold, and 3) quality — output quality meeting product QA, measured by a small eval suite.
[06:57] Samir Rao: We'll need to provide prompt sets and a small dataset to validate. Do you have an eval harness?
[07:04] Luis Ortega: Yes we'll run our Redwood Optimize kits and can run the evals you provide. We'll instrument metrics and share dashboards.
[07:20] Emily Novak: About credits — what does the PLG quicklaunch credit cover? Trials often have limited model access which skews evaluation.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Credits typically cover access to the hosted API and a subset of models in the catalog. We can also grant temporary access to higher-tier model variants for benchmark runs upon request.
[07:45] Anita Patel: If we request higher-tier model access for benching, is that a manual flip?
[07:50] Luis Ortega: We can enable it for the pilot window. We'll note it in the pilot plan.
[07:58] Samir Rao: One more technical: can we bring our own model weights for private? We want to test a licensed model.
[08:06] Luis Ortega: For Private deployments we can onboard customer-owned models subject to licensing; we have an onboarding flow and runtime supports common formats. We'll coordinate with legal if there are third-party licenses.
[08:26] Emily Novak: Ok timeline — what's realistic if we wanted a private pilot start late March?
[08:33] Maya Chen: If we start prep this week, two-week lead for the private pilot is doable. So target start date Mar 22 and run to Apr 5 as a scoped pilot.
[08:45] Anita Patel: That aligns with our roadmap. Also want to know the ops contact list in case the network team needs to approve.
[08:54] Maya Chen: I'll include our install runbook and a contact list for network/infra.
[09:02] Samir Rao: For benching, what telemetry do we get? Token-level, latency per request, error rates?
[09:09] Luis Ortega: All of those. Console gives token breakdowns, p50/p95 latency, trace logs, error classifications, and per-request metadata. We can export logs to your SIEM.
[09:28] Anita Patel: We will want logs to meet our retention policies — 12 months for audit. Can you accommodate?
[09:35] Maya Chen: Yes, with enterprise retention add-on. For pilots we can supply shorter retention but negotiate in contract for longer terms.
[09:50] Emily Novak: Can you show pricing now or after you send the estimate?
[09:55] Maya Chen: I'll send ballpark pricing today in the follow-up and Luis will include bench cost breakdown.
[10:05] Samir Rao: There may be a legal review for private deployment. How long does that usually add?
[10:12] Luis Ortega: Usually legal review is parallel — SOC2 docs and model licensing tend to be the big items. Could be 1-3 weeks depending on customer cycle.
[10:25] Anita Patel: For the pilot success we also want a runbook for failover and fallbacks.
[10:31] Maya Chen: We'll include an SLO runbook and fallback playbook — how to roll back to previous model and route to Hosted if Private has issues.
[10:45] Emily Novak: A silly Q — will we get any SDKs and sample code for quickstart?
[10:50] Maya Chen: Yes, SDKs in Python/Node, plus a Quickstart repo and a runbook to get to first token. TTFT for dev is often under an hour for hosted.
[11:02] Samir Rao: Let's talk about metrics for quality — we want to automate quality regression checks during pilot.
[11:09] Luis Ortega: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and can tie regressions to prompt sets or evals. We can surface alerts if output quality drops compared to baseline.
[11:25] Anita Patel: Network constraints — our corporate firewall restricts egress. Is there an IP allowlist?
[11:31] Maya Chen: For Hosted we provide IP ranges and we support private peering for Dedicated/Private to avoid public egress. We'll share the allowlist and peering options.
[11:47] Emily Novak: Are there limits on concurrency for the hosted trial?
[11:51] Luis Ortega: Trials have conservative rate limits but we can raise for benchmark windows. For production, Dedicated pools remove noisy neighbor issues.
[12:05] Anita Patel: On model updates, do you handle drift or do we manage model rollouts?
[12:12] Luis Ortega: We provide deployment tooling for rollouts; customers control which model version is active. We also provide alerts for quality drift.
[12:29] Maya Chen: Ok quick recap of proposed pilot: 2-week private pilot beginning Mar 22, Redwood provides install runbook, benchmarking script, temporary elevated model access for benching, SOC2/security pack, and network contacts. Highbar to provide prompt set, sample dataset, and list of stakeholders.
[12:58] Anita Patel: Sounds good. A few follow-up items — can you include a slide on cost math per 1k tokens and the assumptions?
[13:07] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll include cost math and the spreadsheet assumptions.
[13:15] Samir Rao: We'll also need instructions to upload the test dataset securely.
[13:21] Luis Ortega: We'll provide an S3 presigned flow or SFTP for on-prem; will include details in documentation.
[13:34] Emily Novak: Who's the point of contact on Redwood for the pilot day-to-day?
[13:38] Maya Chen: I'll be primary AE; Luis will be SE lead for bench and install. Names and emails in follow-up.
[13:48] Anita Patel: Any blockers we should know now?
[13:51] Luis Ortega: Network approvals and legal review are typical blockers. We recommend starting SOC2 and legal review in parallel while we prep infra.
[14:06] Maya Chen: Next steps — I'll send: security pack + SOC2, pilot scoping doc with dates, install runbook, pricing ballpark, and contact list. Luis will attach benchmark script and initial cost calc.
[14:25] Samir Rao: For the benchmark, can we include a few long-context tests and short-chat tests?
[14:31] Luis Ortega: Absolutely — we'll include both and measure p50/p95 and token cost.
[14:45] Emily Novak: Great. Anything else from Highbar?
[14:48] Anita Patel: Not right now. We'll review the materials and aim to confirm pilot by Mar 18.
[14:56] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs.

End Recap (spoken):
- Redwood to send security/SOC2 pack, install runbook, and bench script.
- Target Private pilot start: week of Mar 22.
- Action items assigned and due next week.
